title: Quantum Elements Launches "Orbit" as Qiskit Function for Automated Error Suppression - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantum Elements launched Orbit, an automated error-suppression Qiskit Function distributed through IBM's Qiskit Functions Catalog, combining dynamical decoupling, hardware-aware transpilation, and measurement error mitigation with native support for dynamic circuits, and benchmarks on IBM hardware show large fidelity gains at higher qubit counts.

insights.claim: Quantum Elements released Orbit as a Qiskit Function inside the IBM Qiskit Functions Catalog, giving IBM Quantum Network members an automated, low-overhead error suppression suite that removes the need for manual, circuit-by-circuit noise tuning.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Distribution through IBM's Qiskit Functions Catalog gives Quantum Elements a built-in enterprise and academic user base, a channel advantage versus standalone error-mitigation vendors selling outside the IBM ecosystem.
insights.locator: Quantum software provider Quantum Elements has released Orbit

insights.claim: Orbit unifies three techniques (dynamical decoupling, hardware-aware transpilation, and measurement error mitigation) into a single callable workflow, with each optimization control independently toggleable rather than hidden inside a black box.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modularity lets algorithm teams isolate which technique drives a given fidelity gain, easing due diligence and adoption by technically skeptical enterprise and academic users.
insights.quote: Rather than acting as an opaque black box, the platform offers a transparent development environment where users can independently enable or disable specific optimization controls to evaluate their individual impacts.
insights.locator: At its core, Orbit unifies three complementary performance-enhancement techniques

insights.claim: Orbit modifies submitted circuits directly without requiring pre-calibration runs, extra shot overhead, or extensive classical post-processing, which the article says otherwise inflate execution costs and extend compiling times for quantum jobs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lower runtime and compile overhead directly lowers the cost of running algorithms on scarce, expensive quantum hardware time, a concrete economic differentiator for enterprise quantum budgets versus heavier mitigation methods.
insights.locator: The system modifies submitted circuits directly without requiring pre-calibration runs

insights.claim: Orbit natively supports dynamic circuits and mid-circuit measurements, which the article describes as critical building blocks for fault-tolerant quantum computing, by inserting automated higher-order dynamical decoupling sequences into the idle scheduling gaps created by mid-circuit readouts and conditional feedforward operations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions Quantum Elements ahead of static-circuit-only error mitigation tools as the industry roadmap shifts toward fault-tolerant architectures that depend on mid-circuit feedback.
insights.locator: A key technical differentiator for Orbit is its native compatibility with dynamic circuits

insights.claim: On IBM's ibm_aachen processor, unprotected dynamic Quantum Fourier Transform circuits collapsed to near-zero fidelity at 15 qubits, while adding Orbit sustained process fidelity at 50% for 15 qubits and 29% for 20 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete, checkable fidelity benchmark that technical buyers can compare against rival error-suppression tools before adopting Orbit for dynamic-circuit workloads.
insights.locator: Hardware benchmarks on IBM Quantum processors demonstrate substantial performance gains

insights.claim: On the 156-qubit ibm_kingston processor, raw Bernstein-Vazirani execution failed beyond 26 qubits, but the full Orbit workflow successfully recovered the target hidden bitstring at 70 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Nearly a 3x extension of usable qubit count on a mid-circuit algorithm demonstrates real scaling headroom on IBM's newer, larger processors rather than a marginal lab-only effect.
insights.locator: Similarly, during Bernstein-Vazirani benchmarks on the 156-qubit ibm_kingston processor

insights.claim: In logical-qubit experiments using a [[4,2,2]] quantum error detection code on two entangled logical qubits, error detection alone let Bell-state fidelity decay to 44% over tens of microseconds, but combining error detection with Orbit sustained logical fidelity at 95.3%.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows Orbit's benefit compounds when layered with quantum error detection/correction codes, directly relevant to any bet on IBM-ecosystem software positioned for the fault-tolerant era.
insights.locator: Beyond static and dynamic algorithms, Orbit extends noise protection

insights.claim: Quantum Elements positions Orbit, embedded in IBM's Qiskit infrastructure, as an accessible path to scale quantum algorithms specifically across chemistry, optimization, financial modeling, and cryptography.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals which commercial verticals Quantum Elements and the IBM Qiskit ecosystem are prioritizing as near-term buyers of practical, error-suppressed quantum compute.
insights.locator: By embedding these capabilities into the IBM Qiskit infrastructure
